items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.content_html:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

items.content_html: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

items.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
items.content_html: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

items.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
items.content_html: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

items.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
items.content_html: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

items.title: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response
items.content_html: A record heat wave. Five years of drought. A nation under pressure. Germany is running its biggest joint crisis exercise to date to test how authorities would cope with an escalating climate emergency.

items.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
items.content_html: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

items.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
items.content_html: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

items.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
items.content_html: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

items.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
items.content_html: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
items.content_html: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

items.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
items.content_html: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

items.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
items.content_html: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

items.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
items.content_html: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

items.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
items.content_html: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

items.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
items.content_html: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

items.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
items.content_html: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

items.title: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?
items.content_html: NFTs have plunged in value since their pandemic height in 2021. In some cases, they are worth 99% less than they were paid for. Yet tokenization of real-world assets and AI means the curios may yet have a future.

items.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
items.content_html: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

items.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
items.content_html: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

items.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
items.content_html: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

items.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
items.content_html: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

items.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
items.content_html: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

items.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
items.content_html: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

items.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
items.content_html: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.
